title: Temurah 31
description: Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis on the offspring of a tereifa and the chick from its egg, Rabbi Ḥanina Terita on an animal that suckled from a tereifa, why sacrificial animals are not redeemed to feed dogs, and, as chapter 6 ends and chapter 7 begins, what sets consecration for the altar apart from consecration for Temple maintenance, with Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua on unspecified consecrations and the by-products subject to misuse.
topics: 🐄 The offspring of a tereifa: “both this and that cause,” or “a fetus is the thigh of its mother”
🐣 Rav Huna on the chick from a tereifa’s egg, Rava’s ladle of worms, and Abaye’s “on the contrary”
🍼 Rabbi Ḥanina Terita: warm milk from a tereifa every morning
🐕 “You may slaughter and eat flesh”: not shearing, not milk, and not for your dogs
📖 Hadran: chapter 6, Kol HaAsurin, ends; chapter 7, Yesh BeKodshei Mizbe’aḥ, begins
⚖️ The altar and Temple maintenance: substitutes, piggul, craftsmen’s wages and by-products
🐑 Unspecified consecrations: Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua and Rav Adda bar Ahava’s two versions of dividing a vow
🍂 Shavings, fallen leaves, milk and pigeons’ eggs: what misuse covers

a1.he: וְלַד טְרֵפָה כּוּ׳. לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵפָה (אינה) יָלְדָה — מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּטְרְפָה וּלְבַסּוֹף עִיבְּרָה.

a2.he: וּבְהָא פְּלִיגִי, דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם אָסוּר, וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם מוּתָּר.

a3.he: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵיפָה אֵינָהּ חַיָּה, מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ כְּגוֹן שֶׁעִיבְּרָה וּלְבַסּוֹף נִטְרְפָה, וּבְהָא פְּלִיגִי: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר עוּבָּר יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא, וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי עוּבָּר לָאו יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא.

a4.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּאֶפְרוֹחַ בֵּיצַת טְרֵפָה שֶׁאָסוּר. מַאי טַעְמָא? עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אֶלָּא בִּוְלַד בְּהֵמָה, דְּמֵאַוֵּירָא קָא רָבְיָא, אֲבָל בֵּיצַת טְרֵפָה דְּמִגּוּפַהּ דְּתַרְנְגוֹלְתָּא קָא רָבְיָא — אֲפִילּוּ רַבָּנַן מוֹדוּ.

a5.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב הוּנָא: תַּנְיָא דִּמְסַיַּיע לָךְ, מְלֹא תַּרְוָד רִימָּה הַבָּאָה מֵאָדָם חַי — רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין. עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ אֶלָּא בְּרִימָּה, דְּפִירְשָׁא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא, אֲבָל בֵּיצָה דְּמִגּוּפַהּ דְּתַרְנְגוֹלֶת הוּא — אֲפִילּוּ רַבָּנַן מוֹדוּ.

a6.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אַדְּרַבָּה, אִיפְּכָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא — עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיג רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר עֲלַיְיהוּ דְּרַבָּנַן אֶלָּא בְּרִימָּה, דְּאִיקְּרִי אָדָם מֵחַיִּים ״רִימָּה״, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְתִקְוַת אֱנוֹשׁ רִמָּה וּבֶן אָדָם תּוֹלֵעָה״.

a7.he: אֲבָל גַּבֵּי בֵּיצָה, אֵימַת גָּדְלָה? לְכִי מַסְרְחָא, וְכִי אַסְרַחָא — עַפְרָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא, אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מוֹדֶה! וְעוֹד, תַּנְיָא בְּהֶדְיָא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לַחֲכָמִים בְּאֶפְרוֹחַ בֵּיצַת טְרֵפָה שֶׁמּוּתָּר! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי תַּנְיָא — תַּנְיָא.

a8.he: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁרָה כּוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמָא? אִילֵּימָא דְּמִפַּטְמָא מִינַּהּ, אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה הֶאֱכִילָהּ כַּרְשִׁינֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, הָכִי נָמֵי דַּאֲסִירָא?

a9.he: אֶלָּא, תָּנֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא טְרִיטָאָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהֱנִיקָהּ חָלָב רוֹתֵחַ מִשַּׁחֲרִית לְשַׁחֲרִית, הוֹאִיל וִיכוֹלָה לַעֲמוֹד עָלֶיהָ מֵעֵת לְעֵת.

a10.he: כָּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ טְרֵפָה אֵין פּוֹדִין כּוּ׳. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״תִּזְבַּח״ — וְלֹא גִּיזָּה, ״וְאָכַלְתָּ״ — וְלֹא לִכְלָבֶיךָ, ״בָּשָׂר״ — וְלֹא חָלָב. מִכָּאן שֶׁאֵין פּוֹדִים אֶת הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְהַאֲכִילָן לִכְלָבִים.

a11.he: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: ״תִּזְבַּח וְאָכַלְתָּ״ — אֵין לְךָ בָּהֶן הֶיתֵּר אֶלָּא מִשְּׁעַת זְבִיחָה וְאֵילָךְ, קָסָבַר: פּוֹדִין אֶת הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְהַאֲכִילָן לִכְלָבִים.

a13.he: מַתְנִי׳ יֵשׁ בְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ שֶׁאֵין בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, וְיֵשׁ בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת שֶׁאֵין בְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ.

a14.he: שֶׁקׇּדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, וְקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה. קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ חַיָּיבִין (עָלָיו) [עֲלֵיהֶן] מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל, נוֹתָר, וְטָמֵא,

b1.he: וְלָדָן וַחֲלָבָן אָסוּר לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן, וְהַשּׁוֹחֲטָן בַּחוּץ חַיָּיב. אֵין נוֹתְנִין מֵהֶן לָאוּמָּנִין בִּשְׂכָרָן — מָה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת.

b2.he: יֵשׁ בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, שֶׁסְּתַם הֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת, הֶקְדֵּשׁ בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת חָל עַל הַכֹּל, וּמוֹעֲלִין בְּגִידּוּלֵיהֶן, וְאֵין בָּהֶן הֲנָאָה לַבְּעָלִים.

b3.he: גְּמָ׳ וּכְלָלָא הוּא דְּכׇל קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה? וַהֲרֵי עוֹפוֹת דְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הֵן, וּתְנַן: הַמְּנָחוֹת וְהָעוֹפוֹת אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה! כִּי קָתָנֵי — אַבְּהֵמָה.

b4.he: וַהֲרֵי וָלָד קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הוּא, וּתְנַן: אֵין הַוָּלָד עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה. הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּאָמַר: וָלָד עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה.

b5.he: וַהֲרֵי תְּמוּרָה עַצְמָהּ, דְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ, וּתְנַן: אֵין תְּמוּרָה עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה! כִּי קָתָנֵי — אַעִיקַּר זִיבְחָא.

b6.he: הַשְׁתָּא דַאֲתֵית לְהָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן, כִּי קָתָנֵי — אַעִיקַּר זִיבְחָא.

b7.he: וְאֵין נוֹתְנִין מֵהֶן לָאוּמָּנִין כּוּ׳. הָא קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת נוֹתְנִין? אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״וְעָשׂוּ לִי״ — מִשֶּׁלִּי.

b8.he: יֵשׁ בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת כּוּ׳. אָמַר מָר: סְתָם הֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת, וְחָל עַל הַכֹּל. מַאן תַּנָּא? אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.

b9.he: דְּתַנְיָא: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ נְכָסָיו, וְהָיָה בָּהֶן בְּהֵמָה רְאוּיָה לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבוֹת — רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: זְכָרִים יִמָּכְרוּ לְצׇרְכֵי עוֹלוֹת, וּנְקֵבוֹת יִמָּכְרוּ לְצׇרְכֵי שְׁלָמִים, וּדְמֵיהֶן יִפְּלוּ עִם שְׁאָר נְכָסִים לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.

b10.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: זְכָרִים הֵן עַצְמָן יִקְרְבוּ עוֹלוֹת, וּנְקֵבוֹת יִמָּכְרוּ לְצׇרְכֵי שְׁלָמִים וְיָבִיא בִּדְמֵיהֶן עוֹלוֹת, וּשְׁאָר נְכָסִים לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.

b11.he: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה, דְּאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב: בְּעֵדֶר שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ זְכָרִים, אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מוֹדֶה, דְּלָא שָׁבֵיק אִינִישׁ קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ וּמַקְדִּישׁ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.

b12.he: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּעֵדֶר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מֶחֱצָה זְכָרִים וּמֶחֱצָה נְקֵבוֹת, וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: אֵין חוֹלֵק אֶת נִדְרוֹ, וּמִדִּנְקֵבוֹת לָאו עוֹלוֹת — זְכָרִים נָמֵי לָאו עוֹלוֹת.

b13.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר: חוֹלֵק אֶת נִדְרוֹ.

b14.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחְרִינָא אָמְרִי לַהּ, אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב: בְּשֶׁלֹּא הִקְדִּישׁ אֶלָּא בְּהֵמָה, אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מוֹדֶה, דְּלָא שָׁבֵיק אִינִישׁ קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ וּמַקְדֵּישׁ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.

b15.he: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁאָר נְכָסִים עִמָּהֶן, וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: אֵין אָדָם חוֹלֵק אֶת נִדְרוֹ, מִדִּשְׁאָר נְכָסִים לָא לְקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבַּח, בְּהֵמָה נָמֵי לָא לְקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר: אָדָם חוֹלֵק אֶת נִדְרוֹ.

b16.he: וּדְמֵיהֶן יִפְּלוּ עִם שְׁאָר נְכָסִים לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת — בִּשְׁלָמָא לְלִישָּׁנָא בָּתְרָא, הַיְינוּ דְּקָתָנֵי: ״עִם שְׁאָר נְכָסִים לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת״.

b17.he: אֶלָּא לְלִישָּׁנָא קַמָּא, לִיתְנֵי ״יִפְּלוּ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת״! תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: ״וּדְמֵיהֶן יִפְּלוּ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת״.

b18.he: הֶקְדֵּשׁ בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת חָל עַל הַכֹּל. לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? אָמַר רָבִינָא: לְאֵיתוֹיֵי שִׁפּוּיֵי וְנִיבָא.

b19.he: וּמוֹעֲלִין בְּגִידּוּלֵיהֶן. לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לְאֵתוֹיֵי בִּקְדוּשַּׁת מִזְבֵּחַ, חֲלֵב הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין וּבֵיצֵי תוֹרִין.

b20.he: כִּדְתַנְיָא: חֲלֵב הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין וּבֵיצֵי תוֹרִין — לֹא נֶהֱנִין וְלֹא מוֹעֲלִין. בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ, אֲבָל בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת — הִקְדִּישׁ תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת מוֹעֲלִין בְּבֵיצָתָהּ, חֲמוֹרָהּ מוֹעֲלִין בַּחֲלָבָהּ.

b21.he: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מוֹעֲלִין בְּגִידּוּלֵי מִזְבֵּחַ, הָנֵי מִילֵּי גִּידּוּלִין דַּחֲזוּ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ, אֲבָל גִּידּוּלִין דְּלָא חֲזוּ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ — אֵין מוֹעֲלִין בָּהֶן.

messages.text: Continued from 30b: the mishna taught that the offspring of animals whose sacrifice on the altar is prohibited may be sacrificed, and that Rabbi Eliezer says the offspring of a tereifa shall not be. The Gemara has just discussed Rabbi Eliezer’s view of the offspring of animals that were the objects of bestiality, and now turns to the offspring of a tereifa.
Gemara
§ The mishna teaches that with regard to the offspring of a tereifa, Rabbi Eliezer prohibits it to be sacrificed on the altar, whereas the Rabbis permit it.

There is a dispute as to whether a tereifa is capable of giving birth. According to the one who says that a tereifa can give birth, you find this dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis in a case where the animal first became a tereifa and then became pregnant.

notes.he: פלוגתא היא באלו טרפות (חולין נז:) איכא למ"ד טרפה יולדת ואיכא למ"ד אינה יולדת:
notes.en: According to the one who says, etc.: it is a dispute in Elu Tereifot (Ḥullin 57b): there is one who says a tereifa gives birth, and there is one who says it does not give birth.

messages.text: And this is the matter over which they disagree, as Rabbi Eliezer holds that when both this permitted factor and that prohibited factor cause a certain situation, the resulting item is prohibited. Here too, as the mother of this offspring is prohibited, the offspring is likewise prohibited, despite the fact that its father is permitted. And the Rabbis hold that when both this permitted factor and that prohibited factor cause a situation, the resulting item is permitted. Therefore, the offspring in this case is permitted like its father.

notes.he: וליכא לפלוגי בעובר ירך אמו הוא אלא א"כ עיברה ואח"כ נטרפה דהתם למ"ד ירך אמו הוא אירע הטרפות בגופו אבל היכא דנטרפה ולבסוף עיברה ליכא למימר ירך אמו הוא שהרי יש בו צד היתר אלא בזה וזה גורם פליגי:
notes.en: Both this and that cause: one cannot place the dispute in whether a fetus is the thigh of its mother except where it became pregnant and afterward became a tereifa, for there, according to the one who says it is its mother’s thigh, the tereifa condition occurred in its own body. But where it became a tereifa and afterward became pregnant, one cannot say it is its mother’s thigh, since it has a permitted side in it [its father]; rather, they disagree about “both this and that cause.”

messages.text: By contrast, according to the one who says that a tereifa cannot survive, i.e., cannot give birth, you find this dispute in a case where the animal first became pregnant and then became a tereifa. And this is the point over which they disagree, as Rabbi Eliezer holds that a fetus is considered the thigh of its mother, and therefore just as its mother is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar as a tereifa, the same applies to its offspring. And the Rabbis hold that a fetus is not considered the thigh of its mother, and consequently there is no reason to prohibit it to be sacrificed on the altar.

notes.he: ומשכחת לה שעיברה ולבסוף נטרפה ובעובר ירך אמו הוא פליגי תימה דאמר לעיל אבל עיברה ולבסוף נרבעה ד"ה אסור משום דהיא וולדה נרבעו והכא אמר דלמ"ד טרפה אינה יולדת משכחת לה בשעיברה ולבסוף נטרפה דרבנן סברי מותר דלאו ירך אמו הוא וקיימא לן באלו טרפות (חולין נח.) דטרפה אינה יולדת ואם כן נימא רבא דלא כרבנן וי"ל דודאי טרפות שהוא תלוי בחיות ובריאות כיון שאנו רואין הולד חי ובריא אין לנו לומר שנטרף הולד עם אמו ואין לנו לפוסלו בשביל פסול טרפות אבל גבי רביעה ונגיחה ודאי כירך אמו הוא ומיהו ק"ק דא"כ הוי מתני לצדדין דגבי ולד נרבע צ"ל שנרבעו ולבסוף עיברו ובולד טריפה צ"ל שעיברו ולבסוף נטרפו דמסקנא היא פרק אלו טרפות (גז"ש) דטרפה אינה יולדת וי"ל כיון דבטרפה לא שייך עובר בענין אחד לא הוי לצדדין שאינו יורד להגיד לך אלא כל היתר הולדות של כל האסורים לגבי המזבח ובנרבע דאיכא ב' צדדין ואינו מותר אלא לצד אחד חשיב ליה בשביל אותו צד המותר ובטרפה דליכא אלא צד אחד חשיב אותו צד המותר:
notes.en:
According to the one who says a tereifa cannot give birth, you find it where it became pregnant and afterward became a tereifa, and they disagree about whether a fetus is the thigh of its mother: this is puzzling. For it said above [30b] that where it became pregnant and afterward was the object of bestiality, everyone agrees it is prohibited, since it and its offspring were both objects of bestiality; and here it says that according to the one who says a tereifa cannot give birth, you find it where it became pregnant and afterward became a tereifa, and the Rabbis hold it is permitted because it is not its mother’s thigh. And we hold in Elu Tereifot (Ḥullin 58a) that a tereifa does not give birth; if so, let us say Rava is not in accordance with the Rabbis.
One can say: certainly with a tereifa condition, which depends on vitality and health, since we see the offspring alive and healthy, we have no reason to say that the offspring became a tereifa together with its mother, and no reason to disqualify it on account of the tereifa disqualification. But with bestiality and goring, it is certainly like its mother’s thigh.
Yet there is a slight difficulty: if so, the mishna speaks of different cases, for with the offspring of an animal that was the object of bestiality one must say that they were objects of bestiality and afterward became pregnant, and with the offspring of a tereifa one must say that they became pregnant and afterward became tereifot, since the conclusion in Elu Tereifot is that a tereifa does not give birth. One can say: since with a tereifa a fetus is relevant in only one way, it does not count as speaking of different cases, for the mishna comes only to tell you all the permitted offspring of all the animals prohibited for the altar. With the object of bestiality, where there are two possibilities and it is permitted in only one, the mishna counts it for the sake of that permitted possibility; and with the tereifa, where there is only one possibility, it counts that permitted possibility.

notes.dh: ר' אליעזר סבר עובר ירך אמו הוא
notes.he: מה אמו אסורה שהיא טריפה אף ולד נמי:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer holds that a fetus is the thigh of its mother: just as its mother is prohibited, since it is a tereifa, so too the offspring.

messages.text: The Rabbis concede to Rabbi Eliezer in the case of a chick that emerges from the egg of a tereifa dove that it is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar.
messages.lead: § The Gemara continues to discuss the dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis.

messages.text: What is the reason that the Rabbis rule stringently here? The Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Eliezer and claim that the offspring of a tereifa is permitted only with regard to the offspring of an animal, which grows from its own space, i.e., even when it is in its mother’s womb it develops as an independent entity. But with regard to an egg of a tereifa hen, which grows from the body of the hen, even the Rabbis concede that the chick which emerges from this egg may not be sacrificed on the altar.
messages.quote: The Rabbis concede to Rabbi Eliezer in the case of a chick

notes.he:
שנולד מביצת יונה טרפה שאסור ליקרב:
ולד במעי בהמה אינו אדוק בגופה אלא תלוי באויר ומעצמו הוא נוצר וגדל והולך אבל ביצה כל זמן שאינה נגמרה אדוקה באשכול וגדילה ונגמרה מגוף התרנגולת. ל"א מאוירא קא רביא לאחר שנולד והולך וגדל הילכך עיקר גידולו אינו מאמו אבל ביצה מגופה דתרנגול' רביא והדבר מוכיח שלאחר שיצאת אינה גדילה משום הכי מודו רבנן לשון הירושלמי:
notes.en: A chick: that hatched from the egg of a tereifa dove, that it is prohibited to be sacrificed. The offspring in an animal’s womb is not attached to its body but hangs in open space, and it forms and grows by itself; but an egg, as long as it is not complete, is attached to the cluster [of eggs inside the bird] and grows and is completed from the hen’s body. Another version: [the animal’s offspring] grows in the open air after it is born, and goes on growing, so the main part of its growth is not from its mother; but an egg grows from the hen’s body, and the matter proves itself, since after it has come out it does not grow. That is why the Rabbis concede. The wording of the Yerushalmi.

notes.he: פירוש ולד במעי בהמה אינו אדוק בגופה אלא תלוי הוא באויר ומעצמו הוא נוצר וגדל אבל ביצה מעורה היא באשכול ל"א מאוירא הוא קרבי לאחר שנולד הולך וגדל הלכך עיקר גידולו אינו בא מאמו אבל ביצה מגופה דתרנגולת קרבי והדבר מוכיח שלאחר שנולדה אינה גדילה שני הלשונות פרש"י:
notes.en: That grows from open space: that is, the offspring in an animal’s womb is not attached to its body but hangs in open space, and it forms and grows by itself; but an egg is joined to the cluster. Another version: it grows in the open air after it is born, and goes on growing, so the main part of its growth does not come from its mother; but an egg grows from the hen’s body, and the matter proves itself, since after it is laid it does not grow. Rashi explained both versions.

notes.dh: מודים חכמים לר' אליעזר באפרוח שיצא מביצה טרפה שאסור באכילה
notes.he: אי ללישנא קמא אי ללישנא בתרא. דהתם במסכת חולין הוויין תרי לישני. אבל באפרוח שיצא מביצה טריפה אי ללישנא קמא לא דמי לולד טריפה דהתם איכא היתרא בגויה דזה וזה גורם מותר באפרוח ליכא היתרא בגווה דאוקימנא התם בביצה טרפה דשיחלא קמא דמגופא דאימה פרשה הילכך אסור. וללישנא בתרא ביצה נמי הויא ירך אמו דמגופא דאימיה היא דאתיא מאשכול של ביצים דמעורה בגופה היינו שגדילה באיסור מגופה של עצמה:
notes.en: The Sages concede to Rabbi Eliezer with regard to a chick that emerged from a tereifa’s egg, that it is prohibited to be eaten: whether according to the first version or according to the latter version, for there, in tractate Ḥullin, there are two versions. With a chick that emerged from a tereifa’s egg, according to the first version it is not comparable to the offspring of a tereifa: there it has a permitted element in it, and “both this and that cause” is permitted, while the chick has no permitted element in it, for we established there that the tereifa’s egg is from the first batch, which separated from its mother’s body; therefore it is prohibited. And according to the latter version, an egg too is the thigh of its mother, since it is from its mother’s body, coming from the cluster of eggs that is attached to her body; that is, it grows in prohibition from her own body.

notes.he: (אבל) [אלא] בולד בהמה דמאוירא קא רבי שגדל לאחר שנולדה באויר העולם וגדל בהיתר אבל ביצה טריפה דאינה גדילה מאחר שנולדה אלא כל גדילתה הויא במעי תרנגולת באיסורא אפילו רבנן מודו דאסור:
notes.en: Rather, with the offspring of an animal, which grows from open space: which grows after it is born, in the open air of the world, and grows in permission. But a tereifa’s egg does not grow after it is laid; all its growth is inside the hen, in prohibition, and so even the Rabbis concede that it is prohibited.

messages.text: @Rav Huna That which is taught in a baraita supports your opinion:

notes.he: אלישנא קמא למ"ד טרפה יולדת ללישנא בתרא למ"ד טרפה אינה יולדת שיחלא קמא שהיו כבר באשכול בשעה שנטרפה התרנגולת:
notes.en: Rava said to Rav Huna, etc.: [his support holds] on the first version, according to the one who says a tereifa gives birth; on the latter version, according to the one who says a tereifa does not give birth, [it speaks of] the first batch of eggs, which were already in the cluster when the hen became a tereifa.

messages.text: With regard to a full ladle [tarvad] of worms that come from a living person who subsequently died, Rabbi Eliezer holds that it transmits ritual impurity in the same manner as a corpse, as a full ladle is the minimum amount of dust from the dead that imparts impurity; and the Rabbis deem it pure.

notes.he: במסכת נזיר (דף נ:) מפרש שיעורו:
notes.en: A full ladle: in tractate Nazir (50b) its measure is explained.

notes.he: ואח"כ מת:
notes.en: That comes from a living person: and afterward he died.

notes.he: דגופיה הוא ועד כאן לא פליגי רבנן עליה כו'. [ל"א ועיקר] דאפילו בחייו נמי מטמא ר"א דאבר מן החי מטמא במגע ובמשא ובאהל כאבר מן המת בהעור והרוטב (חולין קכח:) אבל באפרוח אפי' ר' אליעזר מודה דיקרב דהא גופא אחרינא הוא וגוף זה לא היה במעי הטרפה:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer deems it impure: since it is his body; and the Rabbis disagree with him only, etc. [Another version, and this is the main one:] Rabbi Eliezer deems it impure even during his lifetime, since a limb from a living person imparts impurity by contact, by carrying and in a tent, like a limb from a corpse, as in HaOr VeHarotev (Ḥullin 128b). But with a chick, even Rabbi Eliezer concedes that it may be sacrificed, since it is a different body, and this body was never in the womb of the tereifa.

notes.he: מלא תרווד רימה הבאה מאדם חי ואח"כ מת רבי אליעזר מטמא דגופי' הוא ועד כאן לא פליגי רבנן עליה כו' - עוד פרש"י ונראה בעיני דאפילו בחייו נמי מטמא רבי אליעזר דאבר מן החי מטמא במגע ובמשא ובאהל בהעור והרוטב (חולין קכח:) תימה דבמסכת נזיר פרק כ"ג (דף נא:) בעי הרקיב כשהוא חי ומת מהו ומאי קמיבעיא ליה הא ר"א מטמא לפירוש ראשון ולפירוש שני אפי' לא מת וכ"ש מת וי"ל דמיבעיא ליה אליבא דרבנן דילמא ע"כ לא מטהרי רבנן אלא במת דפירשא בעלמא ואינו מגוף האדם אלא בריה בפני עצמה אבל רקב מודו ובגמרא מייתי למיפשט הבעיא שהבאתי מההיא (דהעור והרוטב) (דף קכח) א"ר יהושע לא אם אמרת במת שיש לו רוב ורובע ורקב תאמר בחי שאין לו רוב ורובע ורקב ואור"י דר' יהושע היינו רבנן דהכא דסברי דחי אין לו רימה דאי לר' אליעזר כיון דיש לו רימה כ"ש שיש לו רקב והקשה הר"י אחי מורי דהכא תני מלא תרווד (רקב) רימה ובמשניות (אהלות פ"ב מ"ב) תנן כזית רימה בין חיה בין מתה מטמאה דברי ר' אליעזר וחכמים מטהרין ונראה למורי דהיינו דוקא כשפירש מאדם חי ואז השיעור מלא תרוד ולא היא דמ"מ שיעור תרוד מאי בעי הכא:
notes.en:
A full ladle of worms that come from a living person who afterward died, Rabbi Eliezer deems it impure, since it is his body, and the Rabbis disagree with him only, etc.: Rashi further explained, “And it seems to me that Rabbi Eliezer deems it impure even during his lifetime, since a limb from a living person imparts impurity by contact, by carrying and in a tent,” as in HaOr VeHarotev (Ḥullin 128b).
This is puzzling: in tractate Nazir, chapter Kohen Gadol (51b), it asks: if he rotted while alive and then died, what is the law? But what is its question? Rabbi Eliezer deems it impure: on the first explanation [when he died], and on the second explanation even if he did not die, all the more so if he died. One can say that it asks according to the Rabbis: perhaps the Rabbis deem pure only worms, which are mere secretion and not of the person’s body but a creature of their own, but with rot they concede. And in the Gemara there, to resolve the question, it brings the passage I cited from HaOr VeHarotev (128b): Rabbi Yehoshua said: No; if you said so of the dead, which has a majority, a quarter and rot, will you say so of the living, which has no majority, quarter or rot? And the Ri says that Rabbi Yehoshua is the Rabbis here, who hold that a living person has no worms [that impart impurity], for according to Rabbi Eliezer, since he has worms, all the more so he has rot.
And the Ri, brother of my teacher, asked: here it teaches “a full ladle of worms,” while in the Mishna (Oholot 2:2) we learned: an olive-bulk of worms, whether living or dead, imparts impurity, the words of Rabbi Eliezer, and the Sages deem it pure. And it seems to my teacher that [the ladle] is specifically when it separated from a living person, and then the measure is a full ladle. But that is not so, for in any case, what is the measure of a ladle doing here?

notes.dh: מלא תרווד רימה תולעה הבא מאדם חי
notes.he: ואח"כ מת ר' אליעזר מטמא אותו מלא תרווד רימה (כאהל המנוגע) [באהל ובמגע]:
notes.en: A full ladle of worms: worms that come from a living person, and afterward he died. Rabbi Eliezer deems that full ladle of worms impure, in a tent and by contact.

notes.he: הואיל ופירש מחיים ודמי כעפר בעלמא ולא מטמא דלא הוי מגופו:
notes.en: And the Sages deem it pure: since it separated during his lifetime and is like mere dust, and it does not impart impurity, since it is not of his body.

messages.text: The Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Eliezer only with regard to worms, which are merely a secretion. But with regard to an egg, which is part of the hen’s body, even the Rabbis concede that in the case of a tereifa, the chick that emerges from the egg is prohibited to the altar.

notes.he: אבל באפרוח שיצא דמגופו דתרנגול [פי'] (היא) הביצה כדאמרן אפילו רבנן מודו דוולד מעליא הוא וכגופה דמי ואסור. א"ל אביי אדרבה כו':
notes.en: But with a chick that emerged: since the egg is from the hen’s body, as we said, even the Rabbis concede that it is a full offspring and like her body, and prohibited. Abaye said to him: On the contrary, etc.

messages.text: No proof can be brought from here for the opinion of Rav Huna, as on the contrary, the opposite is reasonable: Rabbi Eliezer disagrees with the Rabbis only with regard to worms, as he maintains that worms are considered part of a person even if they emerged from him while he was still alive, as a person is called a worm while he is still alive, as it is written: And the hope of man is a worm, and the son of man, that is a maggot (see Job 25:6).
messages.quote: only with regard to worms, which are merely a secretion

verse.en:
How much less a mortal, a worm,
One born of humans, a maggot.

notes.he: אבל ביצה (לכי) אימת גדלה לכי מסרחא וכי מסרחא עפרא בעלמא הוא תימה למה הוצרך לומר האי טעמא וי"ל דאינו אלא לרווחא דמילתא דכי נמי אדם לא מיקרי רימה מ"מ לא דמי לביצת אפרוח:
notes.en: But a person is called a worm, etc.; but an egg, when does it grow? When it rots, and when it rots it is mere dust: this is puzzling: why did he need to state the first reason? One can say it is only to add strength to the matter: even if a person were not called a worm, worms are in any case not comparable to the egg of a chick.

messages.text: But with regard to a chick that emerges from an egg, one can say: When does the chick grow out of and emerge from the egg? It does so when the egg rots, and when it rots it is considered merely dust and is no longer attributed to the hen that laid it. Therefore, despite the fact that the hen is a tereifa, even Rabbi Eliezer should concede that the chick that emerges from its egg is permitted to be sacrificed.

notes.he: אחר שהסריחה הביצה יצא זה ממנה וכשהסריחה פקע איסורא דהואי עפרא בעלמא הלכך מותר זה שיצא ממנה אחרי כן:
notes.en: After it rots: after the egg has rotted, this chick emerges from it; and when it rotted its prohibition lapsed, since it became mere dust. Therefore this one, which emerges from it afterward, is permitted.

notes.he: לישנא אחרינא אבל אפרוח אימת גביל מביצה כלומר אימתי נברא בביצה לבתר דמסרחא דהויא כולה מותרת אותה שעה הוא נוצר וההיא עפרא בעלמא היא הביצה דלא חזיא לאכילה ואישתרית לה הילכך מודי דמותר:
notes.en: Another version: but a chick, when does it develop from the egg, that is, when is it formed in the egg? After it rots, when it is entirely permitted. At that time it is formed, and the egg is mere dust, since it is not fit for eating, and it became permitted. Therefore he concedes that it is permitted.

messages.text: And furthermore, it is explicitly taught in a baraita, not in accordance with the opinion of Rav Huna:
Rabbi Eliezer concedes to the Rabbis with regard to the chick that emerged from the egg of a tereifa animal that it is permitted to be sacrificed on the altar.

notes.he: ועוד דהא תניא בפירוש מודי ר' אליעזר לחכמים דמותר באכילה:
notes.en: And furthermore, it is explicitly taught: Rabbi Eliezer concedes to the Sages that it is permitted to be eaten.

messages.text: If this baraita is taught, it is taught, and I cannot take issue with it.
A kosher animal that suckled from a tereifa is disqualified from being sacrificed on the altar.

What is the reason? If we say that it is because the kosher animal was fattened from the tereifa animal, if that is so, then in a case where its owner fed it vetches of idolatry, so too, should one say that it is prohibited? Feeding an animal vetches of idolatry renders it prohibited only if the animal has been set aside for idolatry; a regular animal is not prohibited by this action.
messages.quote: A kosher animal that suckled from a tereifa

notes.he: והא אמר לעיל דמוקצה הוא ואסור באכילת כרשינין אבל דלאו מוקצה לא:
notes.en: So too, that it is prohibited?: But it was said above that only an animal set aside [for idolatry] is prohibited through being fed vetches, but one not set aside is not.

notes.he: אלא מעתה האכילה כרשיני ע"ז ולא איירי במסרה לעבודת כוכבים לכומרים אלא האכילה הוא עצמו שלא לשום ע"ז ואיפטמ' מינייהו הכי נמי דאסירא:
notes.en: If so, if one fed it vetches of idolatry: this is not speaking of one who handed it over to the idolatrous priests; rather, he himself fed it, not for the sake of any idolatry, and it was fattened from them. So too, would it be prohibited?

messages.text: This is referring to a case where one gave the kosher animal to suckle from the tereifa warm, i.e., fresh, milk every morning. Since the kosher animal can maintain its existence based upon this suckling for a twenty-four-hour period, until the next suckling, it survives only due to the tereifa animal. Consequently, the kosher animal is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar.
messages.lead: Rather, Rabbi Ḥanina Terita taught the meaning of the mishna before Rabbi Yoḥanan:

notes.he: כל ימיו:
notes.en: Warm milk every morning: all its days.

notes.he: על אותו חלב של שחרית מעת לעת בלא שום אכילה אחרת וכשהגיע מעת לעת חזרה וינקה הלכך כל גדילתה ממנה היא ואפילו אכלה דברים אחרים בינתיים:
notes.en: Since it can survive: on that morning’s milk for twenty-four hours without any other food, and when the twenty-four hours were up it suckled again. Therefore all of its growth is from her [the tereifa], even if it ate other things in between.

notes.he: וה"ה בכרשיני עבודת כוכבים אם אכלה כל ימיה שעיקר גדילתה מהן שהוא אסור ולפום ריהטא אפילו להדיוט:
notes.en: That suckled warm milk: and the same is true of vetches of idolatry: if it ate them all its days, so that the main part of its growth was from them, it is prohibited; and on a cursory reading, even for ordinary use.

notes.dh: אלא תני ר' חנינא טירטאה הכא במאי עסקינן ר' חנינא בן אנטיגנוס
notes.he: כגון שהניקה חלב רותח של טרפה משחרית לשחרית הואיל ויכולה לעמוד בלא אכילה מכח אותו חלב מעת לעת שאין צריך אכילה מן אחרת הילכך גדל כולו מטרפה ואסור אבל בכרשיני עבודת כוכבים אינו יכול לעמוד עליהן מעת לעת וצריך אכילה אחרת ומותר:
notes.en: Rather, Rabbi Ḥanina Terita taught: what are we dealing with here, in the words of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus? Where it suckled a tereifa’s warm milk from morning to morning. Since by virtue of that milk it can survive without food for twenty-four hours, so that it needs no other food, it grows entirely from the tereifa and is prohibited. But with vetches of idolatry, it cannot survive on them for twenty-four hours and needs other food, and so it is permitted.

messages.text: With regard to all sacrificial animals that became tereifa, one may not redeem them and render them non-sacred, as their consumption is prohibited, and one does not redeem sacrificial animals to feed them to dogs.

notes.he: לפי שאסור באכילה ואינן ראויין אלא לכלבים ואין פודין לכלבים משום בזיון קדשים אלא ימותו ויקברו:
notes.en: One may not redeem them: since they are prohibited for eating and are fit only for dogs, and one does not redeem for dogs, because it degrades consecrated items; rather, they should die and be buried.

messages.text: From where are these matters derived?

“Notwithstanding you may slaughter and eat flesh within all your gates” (Deuteronomy 12:15). This verse, which is referring to disqualified consecrated animals that have been redeemed, is expounded as follows: “You may slaughter,” but you may not shear their wool; “and eat,” but you may not give to your dogs to eat; “and eat flesh,” but not their milk. From here it is derived that one does not redeem sacrificial animals to feed them to dogs.
messages.lead: As the Sages taught with regard to the verse:

verse.he: רַק בְּכׇל־אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ תִּזְבַּח ׀ וְאָכַלְתָּ בָשָׂר כְּבִרְכַּת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן־לְךָ בְּכׇל־שְׁעָרֶיךָ הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יֹאכְלֶנּוּ כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל׃
verse.en: But whenever you desire, you may slaughter and eat meat in any of your settlements, according to the blessing that the ETERNAL your God has granted you. The impure and the pure alike may partake of it, as of the gazelle and the deer.

notes.he: בפסולי המוקדשין מוקמינן לה בסיפרי דבי רב:
notes.en: “Notwithstanding … after all the desire of your soul … flesh”: we establish this verse as referring to disqualified consecrated animals, in the Sifrei of the house of Rav.

notes.he: בפסולי המוקדשים קא מיירי:
notes.en: As the Sages taught: “Notwithstanding, after all the desire of your soul”: it is speaking of disqualified consecrated animals.

notes.he: אבל אי אתה רשאי לגזוז בהן:
notes.en: “You may slaughter,” but not shearing: you are not permitted to shear them.

notes.he: ואכלת אתה ולא לכלבך:
notes.en: “And eat”: you, and not your dog.

notes.he: דאסור לחלב בקדשים דהיינו עבודה:
notes.en: “And eat flesh,” but not milk: for it is prohibited to milk consecrated animals, since that is labor.

messages.text: “You may slaughter and eat,” this teaches that you have permission to derive benefit from them only from the time of slaughter and onward, i.e., those benefits that come after slaughter, such as the consumption of its flesh, are permitted. But one may not derive benefit from their shearing or their milk, as these occur even when the animal is alive.
messages.lead: There are those who state a different version:

notes.dh: איכא דאמרי תזבח ואכלת בשר אין לך בו היתר אכילה אלא משעת זביחה
notes.he: לאפוקי חלב וגיזה דהנאה דמחיים היא אבל פודין את הקדשים להאכילן לכלבים ולא מייתר ליה לואכלת למדרש ולא לכלביך ומהך דרשא משמע דלכלביך שפיר דמי דהכי משמע אתה לא תאכל קודם זביחה כלומר לא תתהני מחיים אבל כלביך דלאחר מיתה הוא אפי' בלא זביחה שפיר דמי ופודין את הקדשים להאכילן לכלבים תרי תנאי נינהו והכי מוקמינן (בשחיטת חולין) (דף קב):
notes.en: Some say: “You may slaughter and eat flesh,” you have no permission to eat them except from the time of slaughter: this excludes milk and shearing, which are a benefit from it while alive. But one may redeem consecrated animals to feed them to dogs, since “and eat” is not left over for him to expound “and not your dogs.” And from this exposition it is implied that for your dogs it is fine, for this is what it means: you may not eat before slaughter, that is, you may not benefit from it while it is alive; but your dogs, which comes after death, is fine even without slaughter. And whether one may redeem consecrated animals to feed them to dogs is a dispute of two tanna’im, and so we establish it in Shechitat Ḥullin (102a).

notes.he: איכא דאמרי תזבח ואכלת כוליה להכי אתא דאין לך בהן היתר אלא משעת זביחה ואילך דראוי לאכילה אבל קודם לכן אסורה לגיזה ולעבודה. וכיון דלא דריש ואכלת למעט אלמא קסבר פודין את הקדשים וכו':
notes.en: From here, that one may not redeem, etc. Some say: “You may slaughter and eat” comes entirely to teach that you have permission with them only from the time of slaughter onward, when it is fit to be eaten, but before then it is prohibited for shearing and for labor. And since he does not expound “and eat” to exclude, evidently he holds that one may redeem consecrated animals, etc.

messages.text: It can be inferred from here that the tanna of this baraita maintains that one may redeem sacrificial animals to feed them to dogs, as this occurs after the slaughter.

notes.he: הדרן עלך כל האסורין:
notes.en: We will return to you, Kol HaAsurin.

messages.text: הדרן עלך כל האסורין · Hadran alakh Kol HaAsurin: we will return to you, chapter 6, “All [Animals Whose Sacrifice on the Altar Is] Prohibited.”

Chapter 7 · יש בקדשי מזבח · Yesh BeKodshei Mizbe’aḥ: what applies to animals consecrated for the altar and not to items consecrated for Temple maintenance, and what applies to Temple maintenance and not to the altar.
Mishna

There are elements that apply to animals consecrated for the altar that do not apply to items consecrated for Temple maintenance, and there are elements that apply to items consecrated for Temple maintenance that do not apply to animals consecrated for the altar.

One element exclusive to animals consecrated for the altar is that animals consecrated for the altar render an animal exchanged for them a substitute, and items consecrated for Temple maintenance do not render an animal exchanged for them a substitute.

notes.he: ממעטינן להו בשילהי פ"ק (לעיל תמורה יג.) דלא עבדי תמורה:
notes.en: Mishna: items consecrated for Temple maintenance: we exclude them at the end of the first chapter (above, Temurah 13a) from rendering a substitute.

notes.he: קדשי בדק הבית אין עושין תמורה דלא איקרו קרבן ועוד דלא קדשי אלא לדמים וולדן וחלבן אסור לאחר פדיונן. כדאוקמינן התם במסכת בכורות בפרק שני כגון דאיעבר לפני פדיונן ואיתליד לאחר פדיונן:
notes.en: There are elements that apply to items consecrated for the altar, etc.: items consecrated for Temple maintenance do not render a substitute, since they are not called an “offering”; and furthermore, they are consecrated only for their value. And their offspring and their milk are prohibited after their redemption, as we established there in tractate Bekhorot, in the second chapter: where it became pregnant before its redemption and gave birth after its redemption.

messages.text: In addition, if one slaughters an animal consecrated for the altar with the intention to eat it beyond its designated time, or if he ate the offering after its designated time, or if he ate the offering while ritually impure, he is liable to receive karet for eating it due to violation of the prohibitions of piggul, notar, and eating while ritually impure, respectively.

notes.he: בשלמים כתיבי ובפ"ק דיבמות (דף ז.) מפרש שלמים בכלל כל הקדשים היו ולמה יצאו להקיש אליהן ולומר לך מה שלמים מיוחדין קדשי מזבח אף כל קדשי מזבח:
notes.en: Piggul, notar and impure, etc.: these are written with regard to peace offerings, and in the first chapter of Yevamot (7a) it explains: peace offerings were included among all the consecrated items, so why were they singled out? To compare to them and tell you: just as peace offerings are distinctive in being consecrated for the altar, so too all items consecrated for the altar.

notes.dh: מתני' יש בקדשי מזבח [וכו'] (אין בהן) משום פיגול
notes.he: כדאמר ס"פ ב"ש בזבחים (דף מו.) ג' כריתות בשלמים למה אחת לכלל ואחת לפרט כלומר לדון בדבר שהיה בכלל ויצא מן הכלל שהיו מרוחקים ומה שלמים קדשי מזבח אף כל קדשי מזבח ונותר עון עון מפיגול וטמא חילול חילול מנותר:
notes.en: Mishna: There are elements that apply to items consecrated for the altar … [liability] due to piggul: as it says at the end of chapter Beit Shammai in Zevaḥim (46a): why are there three [statements of] karet with peace offerings? One for the general rule and one for the particular, that is, to apply the principle of something that was included in the general rule and left it (the text adds: “that were distant”): just as peace offerings are consecrated for the altar, so too all items consecrated for the altar. And notar is derived from piggul through the verbal analogy “iniquity”–“iniquity,” and impurity from notar through the verbal analogy “profanation”–“profanation.”

messages.text: If animals consecrated for the altar became pregnant and then became blemished and gave birth after redemption, their offspring and their milk are forbidden after their redemption. And one who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard is liable to receive karet.

notes.he: נפקא לן לעיל בס"פ כל האסורין בשר ולא חלב. ולדן מפרש בפ"ב דבכורות (דף יד.) בדאיעבר לפני פדיונה ואתיליד לאחר פדיונה דלית ליה תקנתא ליקרבינהו מכח קדושה דחויה אתי ליפרקינהו לא אלימי למתפס פדיונן אבל נתעבר לאחר פדיונה ולד צבי ואיל נינהו ומותרין ובקדשי בדק הבית אפי' דאיעבור קודם פדיונם שרו דלא אקדשינהו אלא לדמי ולא חמירא קדושתייהו כולי האי:
notes.en: Their offspring and their milk: we derived [the milk] above, at the end of Kol HaAsurin: “flesh,” and not milk. Their offspring: it is explained in the second chapter of Bekhorot (14a) as where it became pregnant before its redemption and gave birth after its redemption, for which there is no remedy: to sacrifice them is impossible, since they come by virtue of a rejected sanctity; to redeem them, [the mother’s redemption] was not strong enough to take hold of them. But if it became pregnant after its redemption, they are the offspring of a gazelle and a deer, and permitted. And with items consecrated for Temple maintenance, even where it became pregnant before their redemption they are permitted, since they were consecrated only for their value, and their sanctity is not so severe.

notes.he: בבכורות (דף יד.) מוקי לה באיעבור קודם פדיונם ואוליד לאחר פדיונם דאי איעבור ואוליד קודם פדיונם אמר לעיל בפרק אלו קדשים (תמורה דף יז:) אם לרבות ולד בעלי מומין או ליקרב למאן דאית ליה או לרעייה למאן דאית ליה ואי איעבור לאחר פדיונם ולד איל וצבי מיקרו אלא ודאי מיירי דאיעבור קודם פדיונם ואוליד לאחר פדיונם דלא מהני להו פדיון אמן שהן תמימים במעי אמן אפי' אם יפול בהן מום כשיולדו אינן מותרין כדתניא התם דלא אלימי למיתפס פדיונם והם קדושין דכיון דאיעבור לפני פדיונם קדשו מיד למ"ד במעי אמן הם קדושים ואפי' למאן דאמר בהוייתן ובשעת הויית אמן חולין מכל מקום תפסינהו קדושה בשעת הוייתן:
notes.en: Their offspring and their milk are prohibited after their redemption: in Bekhorot (14a) it establishes this as where it became pregnant before their redemption and gave birth after their redemption. For if it became pregnant and gave birth before their redemption, it said above in chapter Elu Kodashim (Temurah 17b): “if” comes to include the offspring of blemished animals, either to be sacrificed, according to the one who holds so, or to graze, according to the one who holds so. And if it became pregnant after their redemption, they are called the offspring of a deer and a gazelle. Rather, it is certainly speaking of where it became pregnant before their redemption and gave birth after their redemption, for their mothers’ redemption does not help them, since they are unblemished in their mothers’ womb; even if a blemish befalls them once they are born they are not permitted, as is taught there, since [the redemption] is not strong enough to take hold of them. And they are sacred: since it became pregnant before their redemption, they became sacred at once, according to the one who says they are sacred in their mothers’ womb; and even according to the one who says [they become sacred] at their birth, when at the time of their birth their mothers are non-sacred, in any case sanctity took hold of them at their birth.

messages.text: And the Temple treasurer does not give compensation to craftsmen from money designated for purchasing animals consecrated for the altar. And in all these instances, that is not so with regard to money consecrated for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: ואין נותנין מהן לאומנין (בבאין) [בעד] שכרן שבונין ביהמ"ק:
notes.en: And one does not give from them to the craftsmen as the wages of those who build the Temple.

messages.text: There are elements that apply to items consecrated for Temple maintenance that do not apply to animals consecrated for the altar, in that unspecified consecrations are designated for Temple maintenance; consecration for Temple maintenance takes effect on all items;

notes.he: אפי' על האבנים ועל העצים:
notes.en: Takes effect on everything: even on stones and on wood.

messages.text: and one is liable to bring a guilt offering and pay an additional payment of one-fifth for misuse of consecrated property, not only for the items themselves, but for their by-products, e.g., milk of a consecrated animal or eggs of a consecrated chicken; and there is no benefit for the owner from items consecrated for Temple maintenance, in contrast to some animals consecrated for the altar, e.g., a peace offering, from which there is benefit for the owner.

notes.he: מפרש טעמא בגמ':
notes.en: And one is liable for misuse of their by-products: the Gemara explains the reason.

notes.he: בהקדש בדק הבית:
notes.en: And there is no benefit for the priests [our mishna reads “for the owner”] from them: in consecration for Temple maintenance.

messages.caption: The mishna’s two lists: what applies only to animals consecrated for the altar, and what applies only to items consecrated for Temple maintenance.

messages.text: Gemara

And is it an established principle that anything consecrated for the altar renders an animal exchanged for it a substitute? But there are offerings brought from birds, i.e., doves and pigeons, which are consecrated for the altar, and yet they do not render an animal exchanged for them a substitute, as we learned in a mishna (Temura 13a):
messages.quote: animals consecrated for the altar render an animal exchanged for them a substitute

messages.text: Meal offerings and bird offerings do not render an animal exchanged for them a substitute.
When this halakha of the mishna was taught, it was taught only with regard to animal offerings.
But there is the offspring of an animal consecrated for the altar, which is consecrated for the altar, and yet we learned in a mishna (Temura 12a):
The offspring of an animal consecrated for the altar does not render an animal exchanged for it a substitute.

In accordance with whose opinion is this mishna here (31a)? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who says: The offspring of an animal consecrated for the altar renders an animal exchanged for it a substitute.

notes.dh: הא מני מתניתין ר' יהודה היא
notes.he: דאמר אפי' ולד עושה תמורה:
notes.en: Whose is this mishna? It is Rabbi Yehuda, who says that even offspring renders a substitute.

messages.text: But there is the case of a substitute itself, which is consecrated for the altar, and yet we learned in that mishna (12a):
A substitute does not render an animal exchanged for it a substitute.

When this principle, that all animals consecrated for the altar render an animal exchanged for them a substitute, was taught in the mishna, it was taught only with regard to the principal offering, i.e., an animal initially consecrated as an offering, not an animal consecrated by extension, e.g., a substitute.

Now that you have arrived at this qualification of the established principle, one does not need to resolve the difficulty from the case of offspring of consecrated animals by saying that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda. Rather, you may even say that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, who maintain that the offspring of an animal does not render an animal exchanged for it a substitute, since when this principle was taught in the mishna it was taught only with regard to the principal offering.

notes.he: בעיקר זיבחא קתני מתניתין דקדשי מזבח עושה תמורה למעוטי תמורה וולד דלאו עיקר זיבחא נינהו ומיתוקמא מתניתין אפילו כרבנן:
notes.en: When the mishna teaches that items consecrated for the altar render a substitute, it refers to the principal offering: this excludes a substitute and offspring, which are not the principal offering, and so the mishna can be established even according to the Rabbis.

messages.text: It may be inferred from the mishna that consecrations for Temple maintenance are given to craftsmen. From where is this halakha derived?
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches that the Temple treasurer does not give craftsmen compensation from money designated for purchasing animals consecrated for the altar.
messages.quote: does not give compensation to craftsmen

notes.dh: הא קדשי בדק הבית נותנין מנא ה"מ
notes.he: תימה אלא מאי עבדינן מינייהו אי לא דיהבינן להו לאומנין בשכרן לחזק בדק הבית ואומר מורי הרמ"ר דס"ד דאין מותר לקנות אלא עצים ואבנים שהן צורך הבנין וקדושתן נשארה עליהן אבל ליתן לאומנין בשכרם להוציאן לחולין אסור אלא מתנדבין מעות בפני עצמן לפרוע לאומנין משום הכי איצטריך קרא דמאותן עצמן שהוקדשו נותנין לאומנין:
notes.en: But items consecrated for Temple maintenance are given; from where are these matters derived?: this is puzzling: what else would we do with them, if not give them to craftsmen as their wages for strengthening the Temple’s upkeep? And my teacher HaRaMaR says: it would enter our mind that it is permitted to buy with them only wood and stones, which are needs of the building and whose sanctity remains on them; but to give them to craftsmen as their wages, and thereby take them out to non-sacred status, is prohibited, and money would instead be donated separately to pay the craftsmen. That is why the verse was needed: from the very funds that were consecrated, one gives to the craftsmen.

messages.text: It is derived from a verse, as the verse states, with regard to the mitzva to build the Tabernacle: “And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them” (Exodus 25:8). The verse indicates that the Tabernacle can be constructed from that which is Mine, i.e., consecrated property. Consequently, consecrated property may be used to pay the wages of a craftsman for work performed in the service of the Tabernacle.

verse.en: And let them make Me a sanctuary that I may dwell among them.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that there are elements that apply to items consecrated for Temple maintenance that do not apply to animals consecrated for the altar, as unspecified consecrations are designated for Temple maintenance rather than for the altar. Additionally, consecration for Temple maintenance takes effect on all items, but not all items may be consecrated for the altar.
messages.quote: unspecified consecrations are designated for Temple maintenance

messages.text: The Master said in the mishna that unspecified consecrations are designated for Temple maintenance, and consecration for Temple maintenance takes effect on all items. Who is the tanna whose ruling is stated in this mishna?

notes.dh: גמ' אמר מר סתם הקדשות לבדק הבית
notes.he: ואפי' בהמה במשמע:
notes.en: Gemara: The Master said: Unspecified consecrations are for Temple maintenance: and even an animal is included.

notes.he: דאפי' בהמות אי אקדשינהו סתם דלא אמר למזבח אמרינן לבדק הבית אקדשינהו דלא כר' יהושע:
notes.en: Who is the tanna: who holds that even animals, if one consecrated them without specification and did not say “for the altar,” we say he consecrated them for Temple maintenance? Not Rabbi Yehoshua.

messages.text: The mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua.
This is as it is taught in a mishna (Shekalim 4:7):

In the case of one who consecrates his possessions without specification, and among the consecrated property there was an animal suitable for sacrifice upon the altar, male or female, what should be done with it?

Males that are suitable to be brought as a burnt offerings should be sold for the needs of burnt offerings, i.e., to individuals obligated to bring a burnt offering. And females should be sold for the purpose of being used for peace offerings. And the money received from their sale is allocated with the rest of his property for Temple maintenance.

notes.dh: ודמיהן יפלו עם שאר נכסים כו'
notes.he: קסבר ר' אליעזר סתם הקדשות לבדק הבית ואפי' בהמה ומיהו כל הראוי למזבח כשהוא פודהו מיד הגזבר אינו פודהו אלא למזבח דאינו יוצא מיד מזבח לעולם כדתניא לקמן בהאי פירקא המתפיס תמימים לבדק הבית כשהן נפדין אינן נפדין אלא למזבח:
notes.en: And their money shall be allocated with the rest of the property, etc.: Rabbi Eliezer holds that unspecified consecrations are for Temple maintenance, even an animal; yet anything fit for the altar, when one redeems it from the treasurer, one redeems it only for the altar, since it never leaves the altar’s hold, as is taught below in this chapter: one who dedicates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance, when they are redeemed, they are redeemed only for the altar.

notes.he: משום דקיימא לן לקמן (תמורה דף לג:) דמתפיס תמימים לבדק הבית אינן יוצאין מידי מזבח ורבי יהושע סבר זכרים יקרבו עולות דלא שביק איניש קדשי מזבח ומקדיש קדושת דמים אלמא לר' יהושע אין סתם הקדשות לבדק הבית:
notes.en: Males shall be sold for the needs of burnt offerings: because we hold below (Temurah 33b) that one who dedicates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance, they do not leave the altar’s hold. And Rabbi Yehoshua holds that the males are sacrificed as burnt offerings, since a person does not abandon sanctity for the altar and consecrate with sanctity of value. Evidently, according to Rabbi Yehoshua unspecified consecrations are not for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: ר' אליעזר אומר זכרים ימכרו לצרכי עולות ונקבות [ימכרו] לצרכי (להביא) שלמים משום דתניא המקדיש תמימים לבדק הבית כשהן נפדין אין נפדין אלא למזבח שכל דבר הראוי למזבח אינו יוצא מידי מזבח לעולם. ודמיהן יפלו לבדק הבית. מדקאמר ר' אליעזר ימכרו ודמיהן יפלו [כו'] אלמ' קסבר סתם הקדש לבדק הבית:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: Males shall be sold for the needs of burnt offerings and females shall be sold for the needs of peace offerings: because it is taught: one who consecrates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance, when they are redeemed, they are redeemed only for the altar, for anything fit for the altar never leaves the altar’s hold. And their money shall go to Temple maintenance. From Rabbi Eliezer’s saying “they shall be sold and their money shall be allocated,” evidently he holds that an unspecified consecration is for Temple maintenance.

messages.text: The males are not sold; rather, they themselves should be sacrificed as burnt offerings, and the females should be sold for the purpose of being used for peace offerings and they will be offered as such, and one should purchase and bring burnt offerings with the money received from their sale. And the rest of the property, which is unsuitable for sacrificial use, is allocated for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: אלמא מידי דחזי למזבח סתם קדושתיה למזבח:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says, etc.: evidently, with something fit for the altar, its unspecified sanctity is for the altar.

notes.dh: ר' יהושע אמר זכרים עצמן יקרבו עולות
notes.he: לקדשי מזבח משום דקדשי בדק הבית הן כולן (לא) לה' ועולה כולה לה' הילכך זכרים עצמן יקרבו עולות אבל נקבות דלא הוו כולן כליל ימכרו ויביא בדמיהן עולות דקסבר ר' יהושע אדם חולק את נדרו:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says: The males themselves shall be sacrificed as burnt offerings, for the altar, since items consecrated for Temple maintenance are entirely for God, and a burnt offering is entirely for God; therefore the males themselves shall be sacrificed as burnt offerings. But the females, which are not entirely burned, shall be sold, and he shall bring burnt offerings with their money, for Rabbi Yehoshua holds that a person divides his vow.

notes.he: כלומר דמאי דאית בהו דחזי למזבח לא שביק קדושת מזבח ומקדיש לבדק הבית אלמא בהמה למזבח ושאר נכסים לבדק הבית:
notes.en: One who consecrates his property: that is, whatever among it is fit for the altar, he does not abandon sanctity for the altar and consecrate it for Temple maintenance. Evidently the animal is for the altar and the rest of the property for Temple maintenance.

messages.text: Evidently, Rabbi Yehoshua maintains that unspecified consecrations are not necessarily designated for Temple maintenance.

And this explanation of the dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, stated by Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan, disagrees with the explanation of Rav Adda bar Ahava. As Rav Adda bar Ahava says that Rav says:
messages.quote: not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua

notes.he: הא דאוקמיה מתני' כרבי אליעזר פליגא אדרב אדא דאמר לר"א נמי סתם מקדיש בהמה למזבח מקדיש לה והכא היינו טעמא משום דאין אדם חולק נדרו חציו לחדא קדושה וחציו לחדא קדושה:
notes.en: And it disagrees with Rav Adda: this, that he established the mishna in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, disagrees with Rav Adda, who said that according to Rabbi Eliezer too, one who consecrates an animal without specification consecrates it for the altar; and here this is the reason: because a person does not divide his vow, half for one sanctity and half for another.

notes.he: דאמר אפי' לר' אליעזר אין סתם הקדשות לבדה"ב והכא היינו טעמא משום דאין אדם חולק נדרו וכיון שיש כאן הנקבות צריכות לימכר:
notes.en: And it disagrees with Rav Adda bar Ahava: who said that even according to Rabbi Eliezer unspecified consecrations are not for Temple maintenance; and here the reason is because a person does not divide his vow, and since there are females here, which must be sold [the males are sold too].

notes.dh: ור' אליעזר סבר אין אדם חולק את נדרו
notes.he: המקדיש סתם אלא הכל לבדק הבית דמה נקבות לא מצי אקדשינהו לעולה אף זכרים נמי לא אקדשינהו לעולה דאין אדם חולק נדרו הילכך אלו ואלו ימכרו ודמיהן יפלו לבדק הבית. והאי דקאמר ר' אליעזר אין אדם חולק את נדרו דזכרים לא אקדשינהו אלא לדמי היינו פליגא דרב אדא בר אהבה דאמר רב אדא בר אהבה כו':
notes.en: And Rabbi Eliezer holds that a person does not divide his vow: one who consecrates without specification, it is all for Temple maintenance; for just as the females he could not consecrate as burnt offerings, so too the males he did not consecrate as burnt offerings, since a person does not divide his vow. Therefore both these and those are sold, and their money goes to Temple maintenance. And this, that Rabbi Eliezer says a person does not divide his vow, so that he consecrated the males only for their value, is what disagrees with Rav Adda bar Ahava, for Rav Adda bar Ahava said, etc.

messages.text: With regard to a herd that is entirely male, even Rabbi Eliezer concedes that suitable animals are brought as burnt offerings, as a person does not set aside his ability to consecrate to the altar an animal fit to be consecrated for the altar and instead consecrate it for Temple maintenance. Even if the owner consecrated these animals without specification, it is presumed that he consecrated them for sacrifice upon the altar.

notes.dh: דאפילו ר' אליעזר מודה דאין עצמן יקרבו עולות
notes.he: אלא כי פליגי בעדר שיש בו כו':
notes.en: That even Rabbi Eliezer concedes that yes, they themselves are sacrificed as burnt offerings; rather, where they disagree is with a herd that has, etc.

messages.text: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua disagree only with regard to a case where one consecrates a herd that has one-half males and one-half females. And their dispute is as follows: Rabbi Eliezer holds that one does not divide his vow, i.e., state a single vow that must be fulfilled in different ways, and therefore, from the fact that the females are not consecrated as burnt offerings, as burnt offerings must be male, it must be that the males are also not consecrated as burnt offerings.

And Rabbi Yehoshua holds that a person does divide his vow. Accordingly, the males, which are fit to be brought as burnt offerings, are consecrated for the altar, whereas the females are sold to those who must bring peace offerings, and the money from their sale is used to purchase burnt offerings.

notes.he: זכרים לעולה ונקבות לדמי עולה דשלמים ליכא למימר דליקרבו בלא פדיון דכיון דאיהו אכיל להו אתי לידי מעילה דמסתמא לא אמר שלמים נינהו וכיון דהקדיש הכל אינו יכול ליהנות מהן:
notes.en: A person divides his vow: the males as burnt offerings and the females for the value of burnt offerings. One cannot say [the females are] peace offerings, to be sacrificed without redemption, for since he would eat them, he would come to misuse: presumably he did not say they are peace offerings, and since he consecrated everything, he may not benefit from them.

notes.he: ור' יהושע סבר אדם חולק וזכרים יקרבו עצמן עולות ונקבות ימכרו ויביאו בדמיהן עולות:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehoshua holds that a person divides: the males themselves are sacrificed as burnt offerings, and the females are sold and he brings burnt offerings with their money.

messages.text: According to this interpretation, Rabbi Eliezer concedes that one does not consecrate for Temple maintenance an animal fit for the altar. Consequently, the mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer either.

In a case where one consecrated without specification only the type of animal that is suitable as an offering, even Rabbi Eliezer concedes that all the animals are consecrated for the altar. Accordingly, the males are brought as burnt offerings, and the females are sold to those who require peace offerings, and the money from their sale is used to purchase burnt offerings. The reason is that a person does not set aside his ability to consecrate for the altar an animal fit to be consecrated for the altar and instead consecrate it for Temple maintenance.
messages.lead: Some say another version of the explanation of the dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua. Rav Adda bar Ahava says that Rav says:

notes.he: כל בהמותיו אפילו רבי אליעזר מודה דאע"ג דאיכא נקבות הואיל וחזיין כל הבהמות למזבח אמרינן סתמייהו למזבח וזכרים יקרבו עולות ונקבות ימכרו לצרכי שלמים ודמיהן עולה הואיל דאיכא למימר כל הנדר למזבח:
notes.en: Only animals: all his animals. Even Rabbi Eliezer concedes that, although there are females, since all the animals are fit for the altar we say his unspecified consecration is for the altar; the males are sacrificed as burnt offerings, and the females are sold for the needs of peace offerings and their money goes to burnt offerings, since one can say that the entire vow is for the altar.

messages.text: They disagree only with regard to a case where there is other property that was consecrated with the animals. And their dispute is as follows: Rabbi Eliezer holds that a person does not divide his vow. Consequently, from the fact that the other property is not consecrated for the altar, as it is not fit for sacrifice, it must be that the animals are also not consecrated for the altar. And Rabbi Yehoshua holds that a person divides his vow. Accordingly, the animals are consecrated for the altar, while the other property is consecrated for Temple maintenance.
According to this explanation as well, the mishna is not in accordance with the opinions of either Rabbi Yehoshua or Rabbi Eliezer.

messages.caption: Rav Adda bar Ahava’s two versions, in Rav’s name, of where Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua agree and where they disagree.

messages.text: And the money from their sale is allocated with the rest of his property for Temple maintenance.
messages.lead: The Gemara discusses the two versions of the explanation of Rav Adda bar Ahava, in light of the statement of Rabbi Eliezer in the mishna cited above in Shekalim (4:7):
messages.quote: the money received from their sale is allocated with the rest of his property for Temple maintenance

messages.text: Granted, according to the latter version, that Rabbi Eliezer maintains that when one consecrates animals and other property he does not divide his vow, and as some of his property is unfit for the altar, all of his property is consecrated for Temple maintenance, this explanation is consistent with that which Rabbi Eliezer teaches: The money from their sale is allocated with the rest of his property for Temple maintenance, i.e., the money from their sale is consecrated for Temple maintenance due to the consecration of his other property.

But according to the first version, that Rabbi Eliezer maintains that one does not divide his vow even when he consecrates only animals, i.e., he does not consecrate some as burnt offerings and others as peace offerings, let the mishna teach: The money from their sale is allocated for Temple maintenance, without mentioning the rest of his property.

notes.he: דאמר רב אדא בעדר שהוא מחצה זכרים ומחצה נקבות א"ר אליעזר אין אדם חולק נדרו חציו להקרבת הגוף וחציו להקרבת דמים ואפילו ליכא שאר נכסים ואיכא למימר דכל הנדר למזבח פליג רבי אליעזר אמאי תני דמיהן יפלו עם שאר נכסים לבדק הבית הא זימנין דליכא שאר נכסים כלל:
notes.en: But according to the first version: where Rav Adda said that with a herd half males and half females, Rabbi Eliezer says a person does not divide his vow, half to sacrifice the body itself and half to sacrifice its value; and even where there is no other property, and one could say the entire vow is for the altar, Rabbi Eliezer disagrees. Why, then, does he teach “their money shall be allocated with the rest of the property for Temple maintenance”? Sometimes there is no other property at all!

messages.text: Indeed, the mishna should be taught in such a manner, and this is also taught in a baraita:
And the money from their sale is allocated for Temple maintenance.
This emphasis indicates that it takes effect even on items that one might otherwise have thought are not consecrated. What does the mishna mean to add by this emphasis?
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches that consecration for Temple maintenance takes effect on all items.
messages.quote: consecration for Temple maintenance takes effect on all items

messages.text: It means to add shavings and fallen leaves of a tree that was consecrated for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: שאם הקדיש אילן לבדק הבית יש מעילה בשפאין אם שפאו ויש מעילה בנבייתו עליו שנושרין בימות החורף והויין לו לזבל:
notes.en: Shavings and fallen leaves: if one consecrated a tree for Temple maintenance, there is misuse with the shavings, if he planed it, and there is misuse with its fallen leaves, the leaves that fall in the winter and serve him as fertilizer.

notes.he: ומיירי במקדיש את הקורה דאי בגזברים שלקחו עצים אומר במעילה סוף פרק ולד חטאת (מעילה דף יד.) דאין מועלין בשיפוי ולא בנבייה והשתא צריך לומר פירוש מאי מה שאין כן בקדשי מזבח היכי שייך שיפוי ונבייה בקדשי מזבח וי"ל כגון מקדיש שני גזרי עצים למערכה:
notes.en: To add shavings and fallen leaves: and it is speaking of one who consecrates the beam; for with treasurers who bought wood, it says in Me’ila at the end of chapter Vlad Ḥatat (Me’ila 14a) that one is not liable for misuse of the shavings or the fallen leaves. And now one must explain: what does “which is not so with items consecrated for the altar” mean? How do shavings and fallen leaves apply to items consecrated for the altar? One can say: for example, one who consecrates two logs of wood for the arrangement [on the altar].

notes.dh: הקדש בדק הבית חל על כל דבר אמר רבינא לאייתויי שפויי ונבייה
notes.he: שאם הקדיש עצים לבדק הבית חל הקדש נמי על שפוי על הנסורת שנופלין כשכורתין אותו ועל הנבייה על העלים שנפלו ממנו מה שאין כן בקדשי מזבח כדאמר במס' מעילה בפ' ולד חטאת (דף יד.) גזברין שלקחו עצים למערכה מועלין בעצים ולא בשפוי ונבייה:
notes.en: Consecration for Temple maintenance takes effect on everything. Ravina said: to add shavings and fallen leaves: if one consecrated wood for Temple maintenance, the consecration takes effect also on the shavings, the sawdust that falls when one cuts it, and on the fallen leaves, the leaves that fell from it. This is not so with items consecrated for the altar, as it says in tractate Me’ila, chapter Vlad Ḥatat (14a): treasurers who bought wood for the arrangement [on the altar]: one is liable for misuse of the wood but not of the shavings and fallen leaves.

notes.he: אפי' בשפויי ונבייה דבדק הבי' דמועלין בהן:
notes.en: Even with shavings and fallen leaves of Temple maintenance, for one is liable for misuse of them.

messages.text: The mishna further teaches that one is liable for misuse of items consecrated for Temple maintenance and for their by-products, but one is not liable for misuse of by-products of animals consecrated for the altar. When the mishna states that one is not liable for misuse of by-products of animals consecrated for the altar, this serves to add what?
messages.quote: one is liable … for misuse of consecrated property … for their by-products

notes.he: הלשון קשה דה"ל למימר למעוטי מאי:
notes.en: And one is liable for misuse of their by-products; to add what?: the wording is difficult, for it should have said “to exclude what?”

messages.text: It serves to add that one is not liable for misuse of by-products of animals consecrated for the altar, such as milk from sacrificial animals and eggs of pigeons.

notes.he: חלב של מוקדשין. גבי קדשי מזבח נקיט תורין לגבי מזבח וגבי קדשי בדה"ב נקט תרנגולת ולא תורין דאורחא דמילתא נקט דאין דרך להקדיש לבדה"ב דבר הראוי למזבח:
notes.en: Milk of consecrated animals: the milk of consecrated animals. With items consecrated for the altar it mentions turtledoves, [which are fit] for the altar; and with items consecrated for Temple maintenance it mentions a chicken and not turtledoves, since it speaks of the usual way of things, for one does not usually consecrate for Temple maintenance something fit for the altar.

notes.he: לאיתויי חלב של הקדש דבהמת קדשים בדק הבית וביצי תורין דקדשי בדק הבית דמועלין נמי באותן גדולי הקדש כדתנן חלב כו':
notes.en: And one is liable for misuse of by-products: to include the milk of an animal consecrated for Temple maintenance and the eggs of turtledoves consecrated for Temple maintenance, that one is liable for misuse of those consecrated by-products too, as we learned: milk, etc.

messages.text: With regard to milk of sacrificial animals and eggs of pigeons, one may not derive benefit from them ab initio, but if one derived benefit from them, he is not liable for misuse. In what case is this statement said? It is said with regard to milk and eggs of animals consecrated for the altar. But with regard to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, e.g., if one consecrated a chicken for Temple maintenance, one is liable for misusing its eggs, or if one consecrated a female donkey for Temple maintenance, one is liable for misusing its milk.
messages.lead: This is as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: רבותא היא דאע"ג דטמאה היא חיילא עלה קדושת בדק הבית כדבר טהור:
notes.en: Its female donkey: this is a novelty, for although it is non-kosher, the sanctity of Temple maintenance takes effect on it as on something pure.

notes.he: דלא חזו הני גידולין למזבח:
notes.en: In what case is this said? With items consecrated for the altar, since these by-products are not fit for the altar.

notes.he: אפי' בחמור של קדשי בדק הבית מועלין נמי בחלבו אע"ג דלא חזי לאכילה:
notes.en: But with items consecrated for Temple maintenance: even with a donkey consecrated for Temple maintenance, one is liable for misuse of its milk, although it is not fit for eating.

messages.text: And even according to the one who said that one is liable for misusing by-products of animals consecrated for the altar, this statement applies only to by-products that are fit for the altar, but with regard to by-products that are not fit for the altar, e.g., eggs and milk, one is not liable for misusing them.

notes.he: כגון ולדות קדשים:
notes.en: By-products that are fit for the altar: such as the offspring of consecrated animals.

notes.dh: ואפי' למ"ד מועלין בקדשי מזבח ה"מ גידולי דחזו למזבח
notes.he: פירש רש"י כגון וולדות ולי נראה דודאי וולדות אינן קדושים מטעם גידולין אלא מטעם דכתיב יהיו לך (לעיל תמורה יז:) אלו וולדות וע"ק דלא אשכחנא שום תנא דאית ליה מועלין בגידולי מזבח דודאי בגידולי קדשי בדק הבית אשכחנא תנאי דפליגי במעילה (דף יג.) אבל בקדשי מזבח לכ"ע אין מועלין ואומר מורי הרמ"ר דשמא היינו זעירי דאמר במעילה פרק ולד חטאת (מעילה דף יב:) המקיז דם לבהמת קדשים מועלין בו ופריך עלה רב המנונא והתנן חלב מוקדשין וביצי תרנגולים לא נהנין ולא מועלין ומדפריך ליה מגדולין אלמא חשיב דם לגידולין ולהכי קאמר אפילו למאן דאמר מועלין בגידולין וה"פ אפילו למ"ד יש מעילה בדם ה"מ דם דחזי ליזרק אבל גידולין כגון חלב המוקדשין וביצי תורין לא:
notes.en:
And even according to the one who says one is liable for misuse of items consecrated for the altar, that applies to by-products fit for the altar: Rashi explained, such as offspring. But it seems to me that offspring are certainly not sacred by reason of being by-products but by reason of what is written, “which you have” (above, Temurah 17b): these are the offspring. And it is further difficult, for I have not found any tanna who holds that one is liable for misuse of by-products of the altar: with by-products of items consecrated for Temple maintenance I have found tanna’im who disagree, in Me’ila (13a), but with items consecrated for the altar, everyone agrees one is not liable for misuse.
And my teacher HaRaMaR says: perhaps this is Ze’iri, who said in Me’ila, chapter Vlad Ḥatat (Me’ila 12b): one who lets blood from a consecrated animal is liable for misuse of it. And Rav Hamnuna objected to him: But didn’t we learn: milk of consecrated animals and eggs of chickens [our baraita reads “pigeons”]: one may not benefit from them, but one is not liable for misuse? Since he objects to him from by-products, evidently he considers blood a by-product. That is why it says “even according to the one who says one is liable for misuse of by-products,” and this is its meaning: even according to the one who says there is misuse with blood, that applies to blood that is fit to be sprinkled; but by-products such as milk of consecrated animals and turtledoves’ eggs, no.

notes.dh: ואפילו למאן דאמר מועלין בגידולי מזבח
notes.he: הכא (נמי) בהני גדולי כגון חלב וביצי תורין דלא חזו למזבח אין מועלין:
notes.en: And even according to the one who says one is liable for misuse of by-products of the altar: here, with these by-products, such as milk and turtledoves’ eggs, which are not fit for the altar, one is not liable for misuse.

messages.text: Continues on 32a with the next mishna: with regard to both animals consecrated for the altar and items consecrated for Temple maintenance, one may not alter their designation from one form of sanctity to another.
